pairedAcceptance.result: PASS (result.passed, controller/smoke/full exit 0; 95 evidence checksums re-verified by an independent audit that re-derives every percentile and memory peak from the raw samples and asserts the candidate, binary, runner, seed and consumer pins)
pairedAcceptance.workload: sequential official then Firenook: cheap smoke, 7,200 s app-shaped soak (two busy sessions plus an idle observer), export/restart, nine browser journeys before and after restart, then a fresh checkout on the default backend and on the documented official fallback; the attempt-13 workload unchanged
pairedAcceptance.stableStateParity: 1 Auth user, 211,205 Firestore documents and 33,352 stable Storage objects (6,688,940,031 bytes) on both stacks after every soak, journey set and restart
pairedAcceptance.soakCounts: both soaks exact: 480 catalogue reads, 240 function dispatches, 1,440 gateway writes, 960 status writes, 2,880 token batches (57,600 token writes), 240 Storage cycles, observer 240 + 120; 0 errors, 0 stalls, 0 acknowledged-state mismatches, 0 duplicate effects

peakEmulatorPssGiB.process: the emulator by name: java (official) and firenook; the consumer's web server is now the largest process of the Firenook stack, so the top process is not the emulator

consumerWebServerPssGiB.note: about 1 GiB at the attempt-13 consumer revision; the same on both stacks

memory.swap: swap emptied before each stack started; the official stack then held 4.8 GB of swap at the start of its soak and paged out 197,643 more pages during it; the Firenook stack held 36 MB and paged out none

hostBytesWrittenDuringSoak.note: whole host; the official emulator keeps its data in memory until it exports, Firenook makes every acknowledged write durable within a second

initialReadiness.note: application readiness including the consumer's own builds and probes

lastEmulatorPortOpen.note: initial / restart; the official emulator opens Firestore's port first and the others over the following seconds, Firenook binds every listener once ready

pairedAcceptance.browserJourneys: 36/36 passes (nine journeys, both stacks, before and after restart), 0 page errors, 0 request failures; the catalogue journey still ends on the watcher's heartbeat on Firenook (99.4 / 98.4 s against 31.4 / 31.6 official) because the frozen runner's synthetic stimulus lacks the observer's filter field: the official emulator notifies a listener for a document its filter excludes, Firenook does not (recorded since the next.4 qualification; not an emulator latency)
pairedAcceptance.regressions: 11/11 harness, engine (cargo fmt, clippy --all-features --all-targets, cargo test), packaging and consumer build commands exit 0
pairedAcceptance.comparedWithAttempt13: official medians agree within noise (write 198 -> 203 ms). harnessChanges.seedRefresh: the September frozen seed no longer exists; the current private consumer seed holds the same logical state (211,202 imported documents, 1 Auth user, 33,353 Storage objects) with Storage 398 bytes smaller and the Firestore export in 44 fewer files; the manifest records both identities and the earlier contracts are checked against the previous one

harnessChanges.rustToolchain: the regression stage runs Rust 1.99.1 with the product's CI flags (--all-features --all-targets), as the product's own CI does
harnessChanges.terminal: the stacks run with FIRENOOK_PLAIN=1 (the terminal screen arrived in 0.2.0-next.4) and the banner check matches the renamed banner
harnessChanges.consumerDependency: a build dependency missing from the consumer's lockfile at the measured revision was installed into the three stacks' dependency trees without a tracked change; the fix belongs to the consumer

standalone.scope: after the paired run, on the same host: Firestore, Auth and Storage only, the same seed, no consumer application, one emulator at a time

queryShapes.runs: 26 shapes, one warm-up and 25 timed runs each, over gRPC against Firestore holding the seed; every result identical on both
queryShapes.note: the slower shapes order or range-filter a 10,918-document collection, or read many keys; Firenook's field index serves equality filters only

grownStore.officialPssGiB: 15.57 / 15.75 (java 15.09 / 15.27 of a default heap ceiling near 15.5 GiB)

writeAB.rounds: next.5, next.6, next.5, next.6, each on a fresh copy of the seeded store: 2,000 sequential writes each confirmed by a listener, then 4,000 writes from eight concurrent writers
writeAB.result: no write-latency change from next.5 to next.6; next.5's first round had a slow concurrent tail

followUps: Functions discovery takes about 6 s inside the runtime for a codebase the SDK's discovery server answers in 0.2 s (the attempt-13 receipt already noted the inventory answering 7 s after the bind)
ordered and range field indexes (the six slower query shapes)

the Functions log line's duration prints floating-point noise (for example 1.6076249999999999ms)
a start on a freshly copied state directory took 3.0-5.4 s against 0.56 s in place (seen in the write A/B, not investigated)
